provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Art: graduation banner
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list materials for banner making, explain the design process, and create a team banner.

Introduction:
We have learned about different art forms and materials. Today we will use these skills to make our class graduation banner.

Content:
A banner is a large piece of cloth or paper with a message or design. For our banner, we need cardboard, colored paper, glue, markers, and scissors. First, we decide on the theme like 'Congratulations Primary Six'. Then we draw the design lightly with pencil. After that, we cut and paste colored paper to make the design stand out. Finally, we write the message clearly with markers.

Class activity:
In groups of four, pupils will design and create a section of the class banner.

Evaluation questions:
What materials do we need for banner making? What is the first step in designing a banner? How can we make our banner colorful?

Summary:
Today we learned how to create a graduation banner by planning, designing, and decorating together.

topics.title: Music: graduation songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing graduation songs correctly, identify different parts of a song, and perform a solo if selected.

Introduction:
We have practiced many songs in music class. Today we will learn special songs for our graduation ceremony.

Content:
Graduation songs are songs that celebrate our time in primary school and wish us well for the future. We will learn 'We Are the Champions' and 'Congratulations'. Each song has verses and a chorus. The verses tell a story and the chorus is the main part we all sing together. Some pupils will have solo parts to sing alone. We must practice to sing clearly and in rhythm.

Class activity:
Pupils will take turns singing solo parts of the graduation songs while others listen and provide feedback.

Evaluation questions:
What are the two main parts of a song? Name one graduation song we are learning. Why do we practice singing together?

Summary:
Today we learned graduation songs and practiced singing both together and as solo performers.

topics.title: Art: portfolio completion
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to select their best artworks, mount them properly, and write a short artist statement.

Introduction:
We have created many artworks this year. Today we will choose our best works to make a portfolio for graduation.

Content:
A portfolio is a collection of an artist's best work. First, each pupil selects three best artworks from this year. Then we learn how to mount these works on colored paper. Mounting means carefully gluing the artwork to a slightly larger paper to make it look nice. Finally, we write a short artist statement explaining what inspired each artwork and what we learned while making it.

Class activity:
Pupils will mount their selected artworks and write a brief statement about each one.

Evaluation questions:
What is a portfolio? What does mounting mean? What should you include in an artist statement?

Summary:
Today we completed our art portfolios by selecting, mounting, and writing about our best artworks.

topics.title: Drama: graduation play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to memorize their lines, use appropriate expressions, and perform in the graduation play.

Introduction:
We have learned about drama and acting. Today we will practice our full graduation play that we will perform for the whole school.

Content:
A graduation play tells the story of our time in primary school. Each pupil has a role with specific lines to say. When acting, we must use our voices clearly and make facial expressions that match our character's feelings. We also need to move on stage properly and remember when to enter and exit. The play has different scenes that show important moments from Primary Six.

Class activity:
Pupils will run through the entire play with costumes and props in the school hall.

Evaluation questions:
Why do actors use facial expressions? What is a scene in a play? How can we make our play interesting for the audience?

Summary:
Today we practiced our full graduation play to prepare for performing it for the school.

topics.title: Music: instrumental ensemble
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to play simple rhythms on different instruments, follow the conductor, and perform as a group.

Introduction:
We have learned about different musical instruments. Today we will play together as an instrumental ensemble for graduation.

Content:
An instrumental ensemble is a group of musicians playing different instruments together. We will use drums, shakers, and bells. Each instrument has a special part to play. The drums keep the steady beat, shakers add rhythm, and bells play the melody. We must watch the conductor to start and stop together. Practice is important so everyone stays in time.

Class activity:
The class will be divided into three groups to practice different instrumental parts before playing together as an ensemble.

Evaluation questions:
What instruments are we using in our ensemble? What does the conductor do? Why is it important to play together?

Summary:
Today we learned to play different instruments together as a musical ensemble for our graduation performance.

topics.title: Art: body decoration art
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify traditional body decorations, explain their cultural significance, and create respectful designs.

Introduction:
Different cultures have special ways of decorating the body. Today we will learn about these and create our own designs.

Content:
Body decoration art includes things like henna patterns, beadwork, and face painting. In Nigeria, we have traditions like uli designs from Igbo culture or gele head ties. These decorations are not just pretty-they tell stories about who we are and where we come from. When creating our own designs, we should respect these traditions and use patterns that honor our cultural heritage.

Class activity:
Pupils will create paper designs for body decoration using traditional patterns and explain their meaning.

Evaluation questions:
What is body decoration art? Name one example from Nigerian culture. Why should we respect cultural designs?

Summary:
Today we learned about body decoration art and created respectful designs inspired by Nigerian cultural traditions.

topics.title: Dance: graduation medley
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform traditional dance steps, combine movements smoothly, and rehearse a cultural dance medley.

Introduction:
We have learned different dances from around Nigeria. Today we will combine these into a special graduation medley.

Content:
A medley is a collection of different songs or dances joined together. Our dance medley will steps from traditional dances like the Ekombi from Cross River or the Zulu dance from the South. We will create smooth transitions between each dance so it flows as one performance. The finale will bring all dancers together in a celebration of our cultural diversity.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice the transitions between different dance sections of the medley.

Evaluation questions:
What is a medley? Name one traditional dance step we are using. How can we make our medley flow smoothly?

Summary:
Today we practiced combining different traditional dances into one graduation medley.

topics.title: Music: original class song
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to suggest song ideas, write simple lyrics, and participate in recording the class song.

Introduction:
We have learned many songs written by others. Today we will create our own graduation song as a class.

Content:
Writing an original song involves creating both words and music. First, we brainstorm ideas about what our song should say-perhaps about friendship, learning, or looking to the future. Then we work together to write simple lyrics that rhyme. For the music, we can create a simple melody using the recorder or keyboard. Finally, we will record our song so we can share it during graduation.

Class activity:
The class will work in small groups to write verses for the song before combining them into one complete song.

Evaluation questions:
What are the two parts of a song? Why do we rhyme lyrics? How will we share our original song?

Summary:
Today we wrote our own class graduation song by working together on words and music.

topics.title: Full dress rehearsal
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform all graduation items in sequence, manage transitions between items, and give constructive feedback.

Introduction:
We have practiced all parts of our graduation separately. Today we will put everything together in a full rehearsal.

Content:
A full dress rehearsal is when we practice the entire graduation ceremony from start to finish. This includes the banner presentation, songs, play, instrumental ensemble, dance medley, and our original song. We must pay attention to timing and smooth transitions between each item. After the rehearsal, we will discuss what went well and what needs improvement before the actual graduation day.

Class activity:
The class will perform the complete graduation program in the school hall with all props and costumes.

Evaluation questions:
Why is a full dress rehearsal important? What should we watch for during transitions? How can we improve our performance?

Summary:
Today we practiced our entire graduation program to ensure everything runs smoothly on the big day.

topics.title: Graduation showcase
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform confidently, demonstrate proper stage presence, and celebrate their achievements together.

Introduction:
Today is our graduation day where we will showcase all our hard work to our parents and teachers.

Content:
The graduation showcase is our final performance where we demonstrate what we have learned in Cultural and Creative Arts. We will present our banner, sing graduation songs, perform our play, play our instrumental ensemble, dance our medley, and share our original song. This is our time to shine and show our talents. We must remember to smile, project our voices, and enjoy this special moment celebrating our time in primary school.

Class activity:
The class will perform the complete graduation showcase for parents and guests.

Evaluation questions:
How should we present ourselves on stage? Why is it important to enjoy our performance? What have you learned from this graduation project?

Summary:
Today we celebrated our achievements by performing our graduation showcase for our parents and teachers.
